newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude sharpens gains on gasoline rally.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude sharpens gains on gasoline rally.

text.p: NYMEX crude sharpened its gains Monday afternoon on a gasoline-lead rally which also pulled heating oil out of negative territory, traders said.
"Gasoline lead crude higher after crude went up on technical buying," said a dealer.

At 1417 EST, January crude stood 0.51 cent a barrel higher at $24.26 after buy stops were triggered above $23.95 and $24.00, traders said. January gasoline was up 1.49 cents a gallon at 66.95 cents while Janaury heat was 0.72 cent higher at 72.40 cents a gallon.
"Gasoline is the star performer," said a Texas trader.
"The gasoline cash market continues to look strong, plus the strike at Elf Aquitaine is helping prices," said Warren Tashnek, vice president at Fimat USA Futures in Houston.

The strike by workers at three refineries of the French oil giant Elf Aquitaine entered its fifth day. The stricken Elf plants make up a quarter of French capacity and three quarters of Elf's European refining network. The arbitrage from Europe to the United States for gasoline remains open, and the strike could lower imports, traders said.
January heating oil was up 1.02 cents at 72.70 cents a gallon.
Crude's gains were also bolstered by reports that a U.N. committee is meeting Tuesday to discuss Iraqi oil smuggling.
"That helped goose crude up a bit, but a lot of this has been technical buying," said a trader.

But, the regulary scheduled meeting Tuesday by the U.N. sanctions committee on Iraq will discuss a variety of subjects, one of which is a four-month old charge by the United States that Iran aided Iraq in smuggling gasoil through their gulf waters, U.N. diplomats said.
The U.N. sources said the U.S. charges are unrelated to Iraq's oil-for-food deal.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
